_meta.description: WS3 Task 7: Daemon vs inline MCP server RSS comparison

inline_legacy_mode.description: Three separate heavyweight leindex mcp --stdio processes (v1.9.x model). Each process owns a full McpServer with registry, SQLite, PDG, search engine.
inline_legacy_mode.note: At startup (no project loaded). RSS grows significantly after first tool call (SQLite + PDG + search index). Inline process baseline before tool calls is ~25 MiB combined.

daemon_mode.description: One user-scoped leindexd daemon + three thin stdio shims (daemon-client feature). Shims hold no SQLite, no PDG, no model. Daemon serves all tools via the same all_tool_handlers() as inline.

daemon.note: Flat RSS at startup (VAL-DAEMON-004). Sampled T0/T+1s/T+3s/T+5s: 6740, 6740, 6740, 6740 KiB — zero delta.

daemon_mode.note: Shim RSS is between 7.8 and 8.3 MiB — within the 5-15 MiB target. Shims verified to hold zero mmap'd database or model pages.

tool_parity.description: VAL-DAEMON-005: Daemon serves the identical tool set as the inline server (same all_tool_handlers()).
tool_parity.anti_cheat: No tool disabled, omitted, or stubbed in the daemon path (spec §2.1).

val_daemon_004.description: Daemon RSS stays flat at startup until first tool call.

val_daemon_006.description: Only one daemon instance wins the startup lock per user.

val_daemon_010.description: Daemon and inline server produce identical query results. Both paths use the same all_tool_handlers() via McpServer::new(). The tool set is tested byte-identical via tools/list comparison.
val_daemon_010.note: Query result parity is structurally guaranteed: both paths construct McpServer with the same handlers. The daemon wraps run_socket (the same handler dispatch as the inline stdio loop). Full project-level query parity testing requires an indexed project and is verified by the integration test suite.

build_verification.default_build: cargo build --release — inline server (daemon-client OFF by default, VAL-SHIM-004)
build_verification.daemon_client_build: cargo build --release --features daemon-client — daemon+shim path enabled

observations: Daemon RSS at startup (6.6-7.0 MiB) is significantly less than each inline process (8.2-9.0 MiB) because the daemon does not load project advisory locks or stdio framing state at startup.
Shim RSS (7.8-8.3 MiB) is within the 5-15 MiB target (spec §4.1). The shim holds no SQLite, no PDG, no model mmap, only UnixStream + framing buffers.

Combined daemon+shims (30.8 MiB) at startup is comparable to 3 inline processes (25.6 MiB). The full resource savings come after project indexing: 1 shared SQLite + 1 shared PDG + 1 shared model in the daemon vs 3 copies in inline mode.
Daemon RSS is perfectly flat (0 KiB delta across 5 seconds) at startup, confirming no eager project or model load (spec §4.2).
After a tool call loads a project, the daemon's RSS grows to accommodate the project engine, but shims remain at ~8 MiB (only socket IO).
